subject: Art & Design
title: Coca-Cola: 130 Years of Consistent Branding
description: A micro-lesson that makes Coca-Cola: 130 Years of Consistent Branding usable.

hook.text: Coca-Cola's Spencerian script logo has barely changed since 1887. The same red, same curve, same feeling for 130+ years.

buildup.text: Coke is one of the most recognized brands on Earth — valued at over $87 billion. Consistency built that recognition.

discovery.text: Their contour bottle (1915) was designed so you could identify it by touch in the dark or broken on the ground.

twist.text: New Coke (1985) changed the formula and nearly destroyed the brand. Customers rioted. Original Coke returned in 79 days.

climax.text: Santa's red suit? Popularized by Coca-Cola ads in the 1930s. The brand shaped cultural iconography.

punchline.text: Coke doesn't sell sugar water. It sells 130 years of shared memories.

quiz.question: Why was Coca-Cola's contour bottle designed with its distinctive shape?
options: So it could be identified by touch in the dark or recognized when broken
To hold more liquid than competitors' bottles
The shape was cheaper to manufacture

details.summary: Coca-Cola has maintained its Spencerian script logo, red-and-white palette, and contour bottle shape for over 130 years. Despite evolving marketing campaigns, the core visual identity remains remarkably stable, making it one of the most recognized brands on Earth with 94% global brand awareness.
details.whyItMatters: Coca-Cola proves that brand consistency over decades builds extraordinary recognition. While individual campaigns change, the visual foundations stay constant — demonstrating that patience and consistency are the strongest branding strategies.
takeaways: Core visual identity has remained stable for over 130 years
Spencerian script, red palette, and contour bottle are iconic
Achieves 94% global brand awareness through consistency

faq.question: Has Coca-Cola ever changed its branding?
faq.answer: The core elements — script logo, red color, bottle shape — have been remarkably consistent. Marketing campaigns and secondary elements evolve constantly. The disastrous 1985 'New Coke' reformulation showed that even slight changes can provoke intense consumer backlash.

faq.question: Why is the Coca-Cola bottle shape so distinctive?
faq.answer: The contour bottle was designed in 1915 to be recognizable even in the dark or when broken. Its organic curves were inspired by cocoa pod illustrations. The shape became so iconic that it was trademarked as intellectual property — one of the first packages legally recognized as a brand asset.
